notes.atmosphere.dust_tau_scale_pred: Assumption: dust optical depth grows in proportion to the cumulative fraction of ejecta re-entering the atmosphere (25/55/85% after 2/8/72 h); the scale is chosen so that at 85% light drops to the 1% photosynthesis threshold (τ = ln 100 / 0.85). The dust cloud reaches a site at ejecta.dust_cloud_speed after curtain breakup. Synthesis: assumption of the project's predictive model (gap in the literature; approved by the user on 2026-10-04).
notes.biosphere.burn3_exposure_1mt: Value for a 1 Mt explosion; scaling to the impact energy: × E_Mt^(1/6) (eq. 39). Applies to fireball radiation within the horizon — not to the IR pulse from ejecta. Synthesis: thermal-effects zone of the fireball for exposed animals (biosphere layer).
notes.biosphere.deciduous_ignition_exposure_1m: Value for a 1 Mt explosion; scaling to the impact energy: × E_Mt^(1/6) (eq. 39). Applies to fireball radiation within the horizon — not to the IR pulse from ejecta. Synthesis: completes the ignition thresholds (biosphere layer).
notes.biosphere.grass_ignition_exposure_1mt: Value for a 1 Mt explosion; scaling to the impact energy: × E_Mt^(1/6) (eq. 39). Applies to fireball radiation within the horizon — not to the IR pulse from ejecta. The resulting radius is a cross-check of fires.ignition_radius_fireball (different method, different sources). Synthesis: vegetation-ignition zone of the fireball computed with EIEP — compared with the literature value.
notes.biosphere.tree_blowdown_partial_wind: Empirical threshold from nuclear tests (coniferous/deciduous forest); for Chicxulub an extrapolation far beyond calibration. EIEP wind is an upper bound — EIEP overestimates overpressure for E > 10⁴ Mt (airblast.overestimate_factor_large); the lower bound of the zone uses the overpressure divided by that factor. Synthesis: damage threshold for the biosphere layer (blown-down forests); from thread 07, EIEP threshold table.
notes.biosphere.tree_blowdown_total_wind: Empirical threshold from nuclear tests (coniferous/deciduous forest); for Chicxulub an extrapolation far beyond calibration. EIEP wind is an upper bound — EIEP overestimates overpressure for E > 10⁴ Mt (airblast.overestimate_factor_large); the lower bound of the zone uses the overpressure divided by that factor. Synthesis: as above — zone of near-complete forest blowdown.
notes.crater.final_diameter: Spread 180-200 km is largely definitional (which ring fault / gravity-gradient maximum is called the rim). 180 km = horizontal-gravity-gradient maxima + cenote ring (Hildebrand 1995). Expedition-364 literature uses ~200 km. Larger values (240-300 km) refer to outer rings of a multi-ring basin, see crater.outer_ring_diameter. Synthesis: the measurement is not contested — 180 vs 200 km reflects the rim definition (gravity-gradient maxima and cenote ring vs ring faults). ~200 km adopted from the Exp. 364 literature (Morgan 2016, Gulick 2019, Morgan 2022), which also provides the crater kinematics used in the simulation; 180 km appears in older papers and databases.
notes.crater.peak_ring_diameter: No opened peer-reviewed source states a single peak-ring diameter; value derived here. Seismic-image Fig. 1G of Morgan 2016 shows peak-ring rocks between ~40 and ~52 km radius on profile Chicx-R3. 3D model peak rings are smaller (67-71 km; Collins 2020 Suppl. Table 1) - see disagreements. Synthesis: value derived by the research team from the distance of borehole M0077A (drilled on the ring crest) from the centre — no open source states it directly; certainty ◐.
notes.ejecta.launch_angle_max_pred: Project's predictive model: angles range from the one that reproduces the literature first-arrival time up to this value; EIEP assumes 45°. Synthesis: distribution of ejecta trajectories on the globe (slower particles after the front).
notes.ejecta.launch_window_pred: Project's predictive model: the fastest ejecta leave the crater in the first seconds, before the transient crater reaches its maximum. Synthesis: launch time of particles in the ejecta trajectories.
notes.ejecta.reentry_layer_altitude: Here: the altitude at which a particle 're-enters' the atmosphere in the trajectory simulation (flash). Braking starts higher; the main heating happens in this layer. Synthesis: re-entry altitude anchor for ejecta trajectories on the globe.
notes.ejecta.t_arrival_7500km: About 33 min (SOVA 3D model, 45° impact). Synthesis: value from thread 03 notes (Morgan et al. 2013, §4.2), needed to interpolate the onset of the thermal pulse at large distances.
notes.ejecta.uprange_far_weight_pred: Project's predictive model: ballistic ejecta far uprange of the impactor are rare; the K-Pg layer arrives there later with the dust cloud, which the trajectories do not show. Synthesis: consistency of the ejecta trajectories with the IR-pulse asymmetry (Morgan et al. 2013).
notes.energy.kinetic_literature: Computed here from published scenario parameters: collins2020 60 deg/20 km/s 6.05e23 J (baseline); 45 deg/20 km/s 7.6e23; 60 deg/12 km/s 4.9e23; 90 deg 4.1-4.8e23; 30 deg 0.9-1.1e24 J. artemieva2017 (2,500 Gt, 18 km/s) 4.05e23 J; artemieva2009 45 deg/18 km/s 6.6e23 J. Explicit older estimate: pope1997 0.7-3.4e31 erg = 0.7-3.4e24 J. Modern seismically/drilling-constrained scenarios at 45-60 deg cluster at ~5-8e23 J. Synthesis: range merged from threads 01 and 03 (lowest estimates ~1e23 J from the compilation in thread 03). Reference-scenario energy: energy.kinetic (derived.json).
notes.event.season: during2022: boreal spring; depalma2021: boreal spring/summer. Both from the Tanis seiche deposit (~50 deg N paleolatitude). Time of day is not constrained by any source. Synthesis: the reference to DePalma et al. 2021 was removed — the reliability of that paper's data has been questioned (During et al. 2024); the independent source During et al. 2022 (Nature) remains.
notes.impactor.diameter: Not measured: it is the size that reproduces the observed crater (transient cavity ~90-100 km, seismically constrained) for an assumed speed, angle and density. collins2020 (iSALE3D, 2630 kg/m3): at 20 km/s 12/13/14/16 km for 90/60/45/30 deg; at 12 km/s 16/17/18/21 km. Preferred 45-60 deg -> 13-18 km. artemieva2017: 12.2 km (60 deg, 18 km/s, 2600 kg/m3). artemieva2009: 12 km (90 deg), 14.4 km (45 deg), 16 km (30 deg) at 18 km/s. goderis2021 quotes ~12 km. Baseline 13 km = collins2020 60 deg / 20 km/s. Geochemical (Ir) estimates are smaller: see impactor.diameter_geochem. Synthesis: 13 km = the size that reproduces the observed crater in 3D iSALE simulations at 20 km/s and 60° (Collins et al. 2020); independently 12.2 km (Artemieva et al. 2017). EIEP scaling laws with these inputs give a ~150 km crater — the discrepancy is documented as a cross-check (crater.final_diameter_eiep, impactor.diameter_for_crater_eiep); the hydrocode is considered more reliable than the simplified scaling law.
notes.paleo.central_american_seaway_open: Deep-water passage between the Americas in Map16; range2022 reports strong flows in the Central American Seaway. Synthesis: the 0/1 boolean value was replaced by a description.
notes.paleo.days_per_year_campanian: Campanian specimen (Late Cretaceous), a few million years before the K-Pg boundary. Synthesis: basis for the day length at the time of impact (Earth's rotation in the ejecta trajectories).
notes.paleo.notes: Bathymetry: modern 6' topo/bathymetry (Smith & Sandwell 1997; BEDMAP; IBCAO) rotated with PALEOMAP plate model; ocean floor 'unsubsided' with Stein & Stein (1992) depth-age relation; shelves/epeiric seas/lowlands hand-edited from lithofacies (40 m grey-scale steps). 'First draft': subducted-plate bathymetry, shorelines and mountain heights uncertain. 1° grid in palaeo-coordinates (361x181 nodes, lon -180..180). Too coarse for the Yucatán shelf and narrow straits - adequate for basin-scale tsunami travel times only. Area-weighted: land 28.3 %, 0..-200 m 5.8 %, -200..-2000 m 7.8 %, < -2000 m 58.0 %; mean ocean depth 3754 m; extremes -5880/+3000 m. Synthesis: the map number stored in the value field was replaced by a description; the methodological content stays in the notes.
notes.paleo.sidereal_day: Assumption: the length of the year (orbital period) is unchanged — 365.2422 × 86,400 s. Solar day ≈ 23.56 h, sidereal day ≈ 23.50 h. Day lengthening by tidal braking from the Campanian to the K-Pg boundary is negligible at this scale (fractions of a per mille). Synthesis: Earth's angular velocity for ejecta trajectories in the inertial frame.
notes.paleo.wis_continuous_in_paleodem: DEM shows the North American interior as lowland 0-200 m. Literature: marine tongues (Breien, Cantapeta) in upper Hell Creek Fm, WIS connectivity 'not presently known' (DePalma 2019); restricted WIS persisted through latest Cretaceous in western Great Plains, expanding as Paleocene Cannonball Sea (Boyd & Lillegraven 2011); Brazos described as 'at the entrance to the WIS' (Schulte 2006; Vellekoop 2014). Synthesis: the 0/1 boolean value was replaced by a description; certainty: contested.
notes.temperature.initial_surface_pred: Assumption: northern-hemisphere spring; in the Tanis region mean winter ~5 °C, summer ~19 °C (paleo.hellcreek_temp_*). Infrared emissivity = absorptivity (Kirchhoff's law). Synthesis: starting temperature needed for the surface radiative balance in the predictive model.
notes.temperature.soil_conductivity_pred: Assumption: dry mineral soil; typical textbook range 0.2–0.5 W/(m·K). Model: homogeneous half-space, flux pulse following the scenario shape (upper bound of heating), no water evaporation or combustion. Synthesis: assumption of the project's predictive model (gap in the literature; approved by the user on 2026-10-04).
notes.temperature.soil_heat_capacity_pred: Assumption: dry soil; typical textbook range 1.0–1.6 MJ/(m³·K). Synthesis: assumption of the project's predictive model (gap in the literature; approved by the user on 2026-10-04).
notes.temperature.surface_absorptivity_pred: Assumption: natural surfaces absorb most infrared radiation. Synthesis: assumption of the project's predictive model (gap in the literature; approved by the user on 2026-10-04).
notes.thermal.ir_duration_melosh: 'One to several hours' — the value is the lower bound; model without self-shielding. Synthesis: duration of the 'Melosh' scenario needed by the pulse model; from thread 03 notes.
notes.thermal.ir_flux_peak_distal_az45: 45° impact. Read from the figure by the research team (±10%). Synthesis: moved from thread 03 notes (Fig. 4 of Morgan et al. 2013) so that the azimuthal model of the thermal pulse uses the registry.
notes.thermal.ir_flux_peak_distal_az75: 45° impact; pulse tail ~10 min. Read from the figure by the research team (±10%). Synthesis: moved from thread 03 notes (Fig. 4 of Morgan et al. 2013) so that the azimuthal model of the thermal pulse uses the registry.
notes.thermal.ir_flux_peak_goldin: Distant sites; above the solar level for only ~30 min, above 5 kW/m² for a few minutes. The paper gives only a range — a central value is not published. Synthesis: separated from the aggregate value thermal.ir_flux_peak (the 5–56 range combines several models) so that the figure and text attribute only their result to Goldin & Melosh.
notes.thermal.ir_flux_peak_intermediate_az45: 45° impact. Read from the figure by the research team (±10%). Synthesis: moved from thread 03 notes (Fig. 4 of Morgan et al. 2013) so that the azimuthal model of the thermal pulse uses the registry.
notes.thermal.ir_flux_peak_intermediate_az75: 45° impact. Read from the figure by the research team (±10%). Synthesis: moved from thread 03 notes (Fig. 4 of Morgan et al. 2013) so that the azimuthal model of the thermal pulse uses the registry.
notes.thermal.ir_flux_peak_proximal_az45: 45° impact. Read from the figure by the research team (±10%). Synthesis: moved from thread 03 notes (Fig. 4 of Morgan et al. 2013) so that the azimuthal model of the thermal pulse uses the registry.
notes.thermal.ir_flux_peak_proximal_az75: 45° impact. Read from the figure by the research team (±10%). Synthesis: moved from thread 03 notes (Fig. 4 of Morgan et al. 2013) so that the azimuthal model of the thermal pulse uses the registry.
notes.thermal.ir_goldin_strong_phase_pred: The paper gives only 'a few minutes' above 5 kW/m² and ~30 min above the solar level. Project's predictive model: peak of 5–15 kW/m² during this phase, then exponential decay to the solar constant at the end of the pulse (thermal.ir_duration). Replaces the earlier 30-min rectangular pulse, which overstated ground heating. Synthesis: bug fix — the Goldin scenario had been modelled as 30 min at peak level.
notes.thermal.ir_pulse_duration_distal: ~5 min downrange, ~10 min tail to the side. Read from the figure by the research team (±10%). Synthesis: moved from thread 03 notes (Fig. 4 of Morgan et al. 2013) so that the azimuthal model of the thermal pulse uses the registry.
notes.thermal.ir_pulse_duration_intermediate: ~2–3 min downrange to ~5 min to the side. Read from the figure by the research team (±10%). Synthesis: moved from thread 03 notes (Fig. 4 of Morgan et al. 2013) so that the azimuthal model of the thermal pulse uses the registry.
notes.thermal.ir_pulse_duration_proximal: Pulse ~1–2 min. Read from the figure by the research team (±10%). Synthesis: moved from thread 03 notes (Fig. 4 of Morgan et al. 2013) so that the azimuthal model of the thermal pulse uses the registry.
notes.thermal.solar_constant: Present-day value at the top of the atmosphere; the Cretaceous Sun was slightly fainter (of the order of a per cent) — here only the 'above solar' reference level. Synthesis: the level to which the IR pulse decays in the Goldin & Melosh (2009) scenario: 'above solar for ~30 min'.
notes.tsunami.sea_level_late_cretaceous: 170 (85-270) m; published estimates range ~40-250 m, the low end from New Jersey margin stratigraphy. Controls shelf flooding, coastline position and inland seaways. Synthesis: an alternative estimate to paleo.sea_level_above_present (+60–70 m, Miller et al. 2020); both values kept as contested.
notes.impactor.entry_duration: Straight-line, without deceleration — for a ~13 km body the speed loss in the atmosphere is negligible (eq. 8 of Collins et al. 2005 gives < 0.1%). No published value exists for Chicxulub.
notes.impactor.diameter_for_crater_eiep: Cross-check: the simplified scaling law requires a larger impactor than the 3D hydrocode models.
notes.fireball.radiation_duration_eiep: Directly proportional to the luminous efficiency η, uncertain by ~2 orders of magnitude (fireball.luminous_efficiency).
notes.seismic.magnitude_eiep: Depends on the seismic efficiency (seismic.efficiency, contested: 10⁻⁵–10⁻³ ⇒ ±0.67 magnitude).
notes.seismic.t_p_antipode: First P-type arrival for a surface source (ObsPy TauP, ak135 model).
notes.site.paleo_lat: PALEOMAP plate model (plate 205), reconstruction to 65 Ma — the same age as PaleoDEM map 16; consistent with the palaeomagnetic latitude (site.paleolatitude).
notes.site.paleo_lon: PALEOMAP plate model (plate 205), reconstruction to 65 Ma — the same age as PaleoDEM map 16; consistent with the palaeomagnetic latitude (site.paleolatitude).
notes.ejecta.arrival_eiep_10000km: Limit of EIEP applicability (r ≲ 10,000 km); beyond it — distal ejecta models.

tanis.name: Tanis (North Dakota)
obs: Approximate coordinates: publications give only 'south-western North Dakota' (Hell Creek Formation); the point is the centroid of Bowman County chosen as representative — uncertainty of order ±100 km.
Event deposit laid down minutes to hours after the impact (< 1 h), capped by a two-layer K-Pg tonstein 1–2 cm thick; the upper layer is iridium-enriched (3.8 ppb).
Deposit run-up of at least 10 m, bidirectional current structures (inland and back), mixed marine and freshwater fauna.
Interpretation: a seiche excited by seismic waves (P, S, Rayleigh after ~6, 10, 13 min) rather than a tsunami — a debated interpretation (connectivity of the Interior Seaway unknown).
Spherules (mostly 0.3–1.4 mm) began falling ~13–25 min after the impact; most fell within 1–2 h (ballistic calculations).
Spherules in the gill rakers of more than 50% of acipenseriform fish; synchrotron imaging: spherules only in the gills, not in the gut — the fish were alive and feeding during the fall.
Season of the impact: northern-hemisphere spring (osteohistology and δ13C of fish bones); palaeolatitude ~50° N.
An independent paper on the season (spring/summer) has had the integrity of its isotope data questioned — not to be treated as independent confirmation.
The grain-size distribution of the boundary layer indicates a large share of fine silicate dust (~0.8–8 µm).
Empirical sulfur estimate from the Tanis section: 58 ± 9 Gt S; distance from Chicxulub ~3000 km.

hell_creek.name: Hell Creek area — Brownie Butte (Montana)
obs: Coordinates of the Brownie Butte summit (OSM); consistent with PBDB records (47.6; −107.0 and 47.5362; −107.0189 for quarry SMVP 24).

Classic terrestrial K-Pg section of the Hell Creek area; 'transitional' faunas turned out to lie in Palaeocene channels cut into the boundary — the record is consistent with a catastrophic extinction.
Empirical sulfur estimate from the Brownie Butte section: 104 ± 13 Gt S.
No or below-background charcoal in six terrestrial K-Pg sections (Colorado–Saskatchewan) — no evidence of a continental fire; the result is challenged as an artefact of sedimentation rate.
General result (not only for this site): the impact occurred within 33 thousand years of the extinction (high-precision dating of sediments around the K-Pg boundary).

beloc.name: Beloc (Haiti)
obs: Coordinates of Beloc village (OSM); boundary-layer outcrops extend ~3 km along the Beloc–Jacmel road — precision ±2–3 km.
Tektite glasses at the K/T boundary: silica-rich glass (melted continental crust) and calcium-rich glass (melted marls) — an impact into a continental shelf.
Marker bed: coarse microtektites and rare shocked-quartz grains at the base; above, marls with tektite lenses — reworked by a later event, possibly a tsunami.
Marker-bed thickness ~40–72.5 cm (up to 115 cm at thrusts) — data from a field guide (not peer-reviewed).
40Ar/39Ar dating of the tektites consistent with the K-T boundary age (numerical values in an old calibration).

el_mimbral.name: Arroyo El Mimbral (Tamaulipas, Mexico)
obs: Coordinates 23°13′N, 98°40′W from the LPI field guide (precision ~1′).
Clastic unit up to 3 m thick within a sequence of pelagic marls deposited at depths > 400 m.
Three subunits: a spherule bed with tektites, microtektites and shocked quartz; laminated sandstones with plant debris (megawave backwash); thin ripple beds (oscillating currents, possibly a seiche).
Iridium anomaly of 921 ± 23 pg/g at the top of the ripple beds.
Alternative interpretation: turbidites / lowstand deposits, not a tsunami, and an age before the K-T boundary — a minority view.

brazos.name: Brazos River (Texas)
obs: Coordinates of the Brazos-1 section (31°7′53.59″N, 96°49′26.08″W); near the Cottonmouth Creek site (31°06′56.58″N, 96°49′57.71″W).
The only sandstone bed in a sequence of middle–outer shelf mudstones; interpreted as a tsunami deposit 50–100 m high.

Event deposit with Chicxulub ejecta at its base (smectite-chlorite spherules, limestone clasts); ejecta layer ~10 cm (5–10 cm in other outcrops); deposition by repeated tsunamis or storms, then reworking.
Water depth ~75–100 m (another estimate: 75–200 m).
After the impact, sea-surface temperature (TEX86) was on average up to 2 °C lower, with two drops of up to 7 °C (months to decades).
Mass-independent sulfur isotope anomalies (S-MIF) in the ejecta — the sulfur passed through the stratosphere.
Rich ammonite fauna (Discoscaphites iris zone) directly below the K-Pg boundary.

gubbio.name: Gubbio — Bottaccione Gorge (Italy)
obs: Discovery site of the iridium anomaly (Gubbio): Ir rises ~30× above background in Italian deep-sea limestones.
The Ir anomaly peaks in a 1 cm clay layer (mean 3000 ppt), with 'tails' of 20–80 ppt above a 12–13 ppt background; a single anomaly in a 57 m section (10 million years).

stevns_klint.name: Stevns Klint (Denmark)
obs: Coordinates of the UNESCO site (a 15 km long cliff); the point represents the whole site, not a specific outcrop.
Alvarez et al. (1980) report a ~160-fold Ir increase above background in Danish deep-sea limestones (the classic Danish site).
Neritic setting, water depth ~100–150 m; a positive sulfur-concentration anomaly in the section.

el_kef.name: El Kef (Tunisia) — GSSP of the Danian base
obs: GSSP of the K/Pg boundary: base of the boundary clay; GPS coordinates of the marker: N36°09′13.2″, E008°38′54.8″.
At the base of 0.5 m of black boundary clay (~5% CaCO3), a rusty ferruginous layer 1–3 mm thick; the Ir maximum of 16.25 ppb is confined to this layer; nickel-rich spinels.

Catastrophic extinction of planktonic foraminifera and nannoplankton at the boundary; benthic foraminifera without mass extinction but with a clear assemblage turnover; deposition at outer-shelf to upper-bathyal depth.

caravaca.name: Caravaca — Barranco del Gredero (Spain)
obs: Above Maastrichtian marls, 7–10 cm of black-grey boundary clay with a 2–3 mm rusty-brown ejecta layer at the base (spherules, PGE anomalies).
Abrupt extinction of planktonic foraminifera and nannoplankton coupled with an iridium and osmium anomaly.
Bathyal setting, water depth ~500–1000 m.

bass_river.name: Bass River (New Jersey, ODP Leg 174AX)
obs: Onshore borehole (Bass River State Forest); the K/T boundary at 384.12 m depth.
A ~6 cm spherule bed directly above the boundary; spherule impressions in the top of the Cretaceous — nearly instantaneous ejecta deposition; ~2500 km from the crater.
Clay clasts with Cretaceous microfossils 6 cm above the spherule bed — possibly clasts ripped up by a tsunami or megastorm.
Abrupt extinction of Cretaceous planktonic foraminifera and burrowing organisms at the boundary.

demerara_rise.name: Demerara Rise (ODP Leg 207, Site 1259)
obs: Coordinates of hole 1259B (9°18.0485′N, 54°11.9448′W); present-day water depth ~2354 m.
A normally graded spherule bed ~2 cm thick (ejecta airfall), spherules up to 2.5 mm; no other spherule beds.
Ir maximum ~1.5 ppb at the top of the spherule bed; foraminifera decline from abundant to rare.
~4500 km from the crater; well-preserved simple stratigraphy attributed to shelter from impact-generated waves.

woodside_creek.name: Woodside Creek (New Zealand)
obs: Coordinates from PBDB (41°55′S, 174°04′E, based on a nearby landmark; precision to minutes).
Iridium 153 ng/g in the lower 2 mm of an 8 mm boundary-shale parting; integrated Ir 187 ng/cm²; enrichment in Au, Cu, Co, Cr, Ni, As, Mo, Fe; Ir/Au = 2.1.
Alvarez et al. (1980) report a ~20-fold Ir increase in New Zealand; Brooks et al. (1984) call Woodside Creek the 'locus classicus' of iridium anomalies.
